Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks — finance here. Short answer: we need a validated VAT number (we check VIES) + a clear statement that this is a B2B supply. If the VIES check passes, the correct accounting treatment for a cross-border business-to-business SaaS supply is typically to zero-rate the invoice and annotate it as "reverse-charge" (customer liable). Our options:

- Option A (preferred for AP): Issue a credit note for INV-2026-06-29 and reissue INV-2026-06-29-R with no VAT, labelled: "Reverse-charge EU supply — customer VAT ID validated". This is easiest for their AP to record.
- Option B (faster): Leave invoice as-is in the portal but update its metadata to show reverse-charge; send confirmation letter and evidence of VAT validation to Novus so AP can self-account. Some customers still insist on a formal credit+reissue.

We will also need Novus to confirm the billing address and company registration number in case local tax teams ask. If they're close to month-end and want payment to go through, Option B plus voucher evidence might unblock them quicker. For our internal controls, we should attach the VIES check result and the VAT certificate to the billing record.

Evelyn — I can prepare the credit note and reissue the zero-rated invoice once Novus sends the certificate. Target SLA: 48 hours from receipt of the VAT cert.

Attachments required: VAT certificate (PDF), copy of VIES check (screenshot or link).

-Michael
